hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a wide street can lead to unpredictable vehicle positioning and higher speeds.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street blocks sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated crossing points for pedestrians to access the park from the residential side, forcing mid-block crossings without protection.

hazards.name: Construction Obstructions
hazards.description: Orange construction barrels and metal plates are placed directly in the pedestrian path, creating tripping hazards and narrowing the walkway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center-left on the sidewalk

hazards.name: Wide Uncontrolled Driveway
hazards.description: A very wide entrance to a parking lot creates a large conflict zone where vehicles can turn across the sidewalk at higher speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Middle ground on the left side

hazards.name: Lack of Protected Crossing
hazards.description: The wide multi-lane road lacks any marked crossing or pedestrian refuge, making it dangerous for pedestrians to cross.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalks
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk markings at the intersection are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the center of the narrow sidewalk on the right side of the street, forcing pedestrians to maneuver around them.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is immediately adjacent to the roadway with no planting strip or furniture zone to protect pedestrians from moving vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of continuous walkway
hazards.description: There is no clear, paved public sidewalk; private stairs and small yards extend directly to the curb line, forcing pedestrians into the roadway.

hazards.name: Undefined Pedestrian Path in Parking Lot

hazards.location_in_image: Center background, the large asphalt area between the sidewalk and the buildings.

hazards.name: Wide Driveway Conflict Point

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along both sides of the street block sightlines between pedestrians (especially children) and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the roadway

hazards.name: Degraded Roadway Pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and wear in the asphalt surface could present a trip hazard for pedestrians crossing mid-block.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars

hazards.name: Blank building frontage

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb line block the view between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the road.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: The large tree canopy and the parked SUV significantly block sightlines between the sidewalk and the roadway for any potential mid-block crossing.

hazards.name: Lack of Natural Surveillance
hazards.description: The blank industrial wall and fencing provide no 'eyes on the street', which can decrease the perceived and actual safety of pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visibility Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The windowless building and chain-link fence reduce natural surveillance and create an isolated environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visibility Obstruction
hazards.description: Continuous on-street parking blocks sightlines between drivers and pedestrians who might attempt to cross the street.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Significant cracking and weeds growing through the concrete apron in front of the building create trip hazards.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Separation

hazards.name: Blank Frontage and Fencing
hazards.description: Extensive chain-link fencing and windowless brick walls create a hostile environment with no eyes on the street.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parking
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides limits sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs visible in this mid-block section.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk at the intersection is worn and difficult to see.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to designate safe crossing points.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at crossing points to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing and Markings
interventions.description: Add painted lane lines to define travel lanes and narrow the perceived roadway width to slow traffic.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install physical traffic calming measures to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential/commercial mix area.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion and Maintenance
interventions.description: Ensure the sidewalk network is continuous and free of construction debris or temporary plates once work is finished.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation and Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the parking lot entrance to slow turning vehicles and shorten the pedestrian exposure distance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk and Signalization
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with a pedestrian-actuated signal or HAWK beacon to provide a safe crossing point across the wide arterial.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions (bulb-outs) at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalk that is clearly separated from private property and the roadway.

interventions.title: Lane Markings
interventions.description: Paint center lines and parking lane lines to narrow the travel lanes and slow traffic.

interventions.title: Internal Pedestrian Walkways
interventions.description: Install raised or clearly marked pedestrian walkways through the parking lot to provide safe, direct access to building entrances.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions and Driveway Narrowing
interventions.description: Narrow the driveway entrance using curb extensions to reduce vehicle turning speeds and shorten the crossing distance for pedestrians on the sidewalk.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Add street trees in a furniture zone or within curb extensions to provide a physical buffer and naturally slow traffic speeds.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain low in this residential context.

interventions.title: Streetscape Enhancements
interventions.description: Introduce street furniture, planters, or public art along the blank wall to activate the space and improve the pedestrian experience.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add high-visibility crosswalk markings to designate safe crossing locations, especially near the park entrance.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or speed cushions to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential context.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Prune the lower branches of the street tree to maintain a clear sight window between 3 and 7 feet above the ground.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and security along the industrial frontage.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Adding a planting zone between the sidewalk and the curb would provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic and improve the walking environment.

interventions.title: Daylighting at Intersections
interventions.description: Removing parking spaces closest to the nearest intersections would improve visibility for pedestrians and drivers, though not directly visible in this mid-block shot.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Widen the sidewalk on the right side and relocate utility poles to the furniture zone to provide a clear, accessible path of travel.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Add street trees along the blank wall on the left to improve the pedestrian experience and provide a buffer from the industrial frontage.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Removing parking spaces near potential crossing points to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Replace the uneven and cracked paved apron with a continuous, ADA-compliant concrete sidewalk.

interventions.title: Vertical Curb Installation
interventions.description: Install a standard vertical curb to clearly define the edge of the roadway and provide physical protection for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Introduce street trees or a planting strip between the sidewalk and the roadway to improve the pedestrian experience and provide a safety buffer.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and perceived safety during nighttime.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer/Street Trees
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and moving traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Infill
interventions.description: Construct a continuous paved sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a safe, separated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Expand the sidewalk width to at least 5-6 feet to provide a safe and accessible clear path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
